`wall s` = newest file the graph wrote in its own ComfyUI output subfolder minus the `JOB start` line. The harness `secs` is poll-quantized (`comm.py POLL_SEC = 60`, the loop sleeps before the first `/history` check), so it prints 120.2/180.2 s steps and is a ceiling, never a cost measure - the v1 lesson, applied here. Copies into the run dirs carry the copy time, so they are never used for the clock.

The v1 queue's VLM raised `start_kept` on 10/14 and `target_reached` on 5/14; the v2 queue's VLM raised nothing, and for the same arms and seeds the answers on those two questions read "no" in v1 and "yes" in v2 (see `review/terrace-retest-v2-2026-10-30/judge_out/vlm/*.json`). That is a measured difference between two 14-clip sets. It is not a quality claim: the only intended variable is the prompt, the judge is a noisy instrument, and on this cell the flags were already shown not to separate arms. The deciding instrument is Max's blind 0-10 scores.

## Instruments learned this queue (kept for the next one)

- A graph with two SaveVideo sinks still makes the runner's OBJECTIVE line land on whichever file ComfyUI reports first: in this queue all three T4c rows reported the **processed** 920x1616 file, in the v1 queue one seed reported the `_raw`. Both files are collected per run dir as `<arm>_raw.mp4` / `<arm>_processed.mp4`, and the judged file is the `_raw`, ffprobe-verified 768x1344/124 with audio. So a T4c run dir holds three mp4s: the runner's collected file (byte-identical to `_processed`, same size - it is the same sink), `_processed` (the record copy) and `_raw` (the file that is scored). 11 B2-family + 3 collected + 3 `_processed` + 3 `_raw` = the 20 mp4s in this root; nothing else was written to a run dir. The scored set is 14: 11 + 3 `_raw`.
- `notes/terrace_retest_v2_render_run_check.py` is the shape brief3/brief5 asks for: gpu_guard, then pytest, then `comm.guard_ok`, then the runner, then a re-read of the run dir's own `status.log` and output mtimes. The runner's exit code alone is never the verdict.
- Judge tools stay unedited and manifest-driven; the driver patches `MANIFEST/RUNS/PROMPTS/OUT` and stages clips as `judge_runs/<tag>/<tag>.mp4`. The prompt shown to the VLM is the prompt that was submitted (B2v2; S8 = B2v2 + the #74 line), which the v1 driver could not do from the v1 file.
